newsitem.title: USA: Gov Pataki wary on $900 mln NYC rail tunnel - paper.
newsitem.headline: Gov Pataki wary on $900 mln NYC rail tunnel - paper.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki said he was not ready to support New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani's plan to build a $900 million freight-rail tunnel under New York Harbor, New York Times reported Thursday.
The governor said, "I can't commit to financing (the project)" at a forum sponsored by Crain's New York Business and New York City Partnership, the Times said.

Pataki's support is crucial as the mayor is hoping that up to 80 percent of the cost of the tunnel would be paid for with federal transportation money. The governor and the legislature decide how New York's share of those funds are spent.

The mayor's main goals in his plan are to speed how goods are shipped to the city, which depends more heavily on trucks than any other large city in the nation, and cut traffic and pollution, according to the paper.
The proposal calls for building a tunnel to run from Brooklyn to either Staten Island or Jersey City, and it also could help make it more attractive for shippers by linking with the rail system.
